content.chapter: Chapter 5: The Yesevî Path and the Mausoleum
objectives: Explain how the Yesevî Path spread and how Yesevî is revered today.

Explain what the burial practice shows about his influence.
Use whose, participle result clauses and with the intention of + -ing.
content.pedagogy: A long, information-rich chapter. A timeline (1166 → 1389–1405 → 1405 → 2003 → today) and a cause-and-effect chain (reverence → burial practice → evidence of influence) help learners process the content and see how the writer moves from facts to interpretation.
anticipatedMisconceptions: Timur ordered the mausoleum; TİKA completed restoration, landscaping and lighting, not the original construction.
The path became part of several other orders; Yesevî is recognized as their spiritual leader.

Use (Activity 4): the story of a monument.

expectedResponses: Timur ordered a mausoleum to be built over Yesevî’s grave, but work stopped upon his death in 1405, leaving the building unfinished. Many nomadic Turks bought plots with the intention of being buried there, which demonstrates Yesevî’s profound influence.

content.chapter: Chapter 7: The Path to Fenâʾ fillâh
objectives: Explain fenâʾ fillâh in the words of the book.
Explain how Yesevî united national elements with religious values.
Classify the qualities to be rooted out, rejected and cultivated.
Use modal passives and not merely … Rather.

Notice (Activity 1): must be rooted out …

Use (Activity 4): building character today.

content.teacherReflection: Did learners support their evaluation with evidence?

metadata.title: Ahmed Yesevî B2 — Teacher’s Book
metadata.subtitle: Pîr-i Turkistan
metadata.estimatedDuration: 13 chapter units of 45 minutes each. Whole-book review pages follow separately.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can follow extended texts about history, ideas and values, and who can produce clear, detailed explanations, evaluations and arguments.
metadata.purpose: Develop evidence-based B2 reading, listening, speaking and writing through Ahmed Yesevî: his life, masters and mausoleum, language and identity, the path to fenâʾ fillâh, education of love, the movement and its works, the meaning of wisdom, the civilization of wisdom and lines from the Dîvân, using the Language Focus attached to every story chapter.
metadata.approachDesc: Every story chapter follows the TYMM route. YDAB1 listening and YDAB2 reading establish meaning and evidence; the Quick Challenge checks comprehension. Grammar is then learned inductively: in the Language Focus, learners first NOTICE a form in a real chapter sentence and work out what it does, then BUILD it in controlled, meaningful practice, and finally USE it in connected YDAB3 speaking and YDAB4 writing about their own world. At B2, learners also notice how the writer signals certainty (It is believed that / attributed to / it should be noted that / probably) and builds an argument, and they use these forms in their own writing.
metadata.assessmentEvidence: 13 Quick Challenges, text-evidence checks, chapter Language Focus tasks (Notice → Build → Use), exit tickets, Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review and Final Challenge.

formative: Short spoken and written Use tasks

readingFramework.before: Activate only what the chapter needs: a short question, a map, a date or a picture.
readingFramework.during: Listen first for gist (when the audio is ready), then read and follow the chapter’s own structure: definitions, a succession of masters, a building history, a concept, an argument, quotations with sources or poem lines.
readingFramework.after: Complete the Quick Challenge, then the chapter’s Language Focus (notice → build → use), then a connected B2 transfer: an explanation, evaluation or argument about the learners’ own world.

vocabularyApproach.selection: Word Notes are the bold words of the teacher-approved text. Prioritize them and the words needed for the chapter’s key idea.
vocabularyApproach.method: Infer meaning from context or a picture before any direct explanation.
vocabularyApproach.recycling: Reuse vocabulary in Language Focus tasks, exit tickets and the Language Review.

metadata.grammarApproach: Inductive and text-based. Start from the story sentence, ask a meaning question (What does this form tell us? How certain is the writer?), let learners formulate the rule, then confirm it and practice it in context. B2 targets include participle clauses, cleft sentences, modal passives, inversion, whose-clauses, noun clauses (The fact that) and formal linkers. Rule explanations appear in the app only after learners answer.
grammarSequence: Ch1: reduced relative clause (called …) · both … and · one of the + plural noun · parallel infinitives
Ch2: Having + past participle · was raised · at a time when · It is believed that
Ch3: cleft sentence (This was … who) · Following + noun · come under someone’s guidance · parallel past verbs
Ch4: through + noun (means) · as well as + noun phrase · in the vicinity of
Ch5: whose · participle result clause (leaving …) · upon + noun · with the intention of + -ing · have been completed
Ch6: while (contrast) · Although … , thus + -ing · participle clause of purpose (striving to …)
Ch7: modal passive (must be rooted out / rejected / cultivated) · not merely … Rather · manifest itself
Ch8: not only … but also · inversion after Among … · only possible by + -ing · so that
Ch9: reduced passive clause (initiated by …) · attributed to · it should be noted that · Since (= because) · probably
Ch10: Whether … or … · It is impossible for … to · As long as · to ensure that · mere + noun
Ch11: The fact that + clause · those who + plural verb · regardless of · inseparable from · not … either
Ch12: transform … into · despite + noun phrase · To this day + present simple · who (defining)
Ch13: It would be better for … to + verb · Although · having + past participle

skillsFocus.listening: TYMM YDAB1: follow extended narration for gist, attributed views and key details.
skillsFocus.reading: TYMM YDAB2: identify definitions, arguments, degrees of certainty, concepts and quotations with their sources.
skillsFocus.speaking: TYMM YDAB3: explain and evaluate ideas, compare past and present and present balanced positions.
skillsFocus.writing: TYMM YDAB4: produce clear, detailed B2 paragraphs and short arguments with evidence, hedging and balanced conclusions.

valuesFocus: D14 Respect — Respect for teachers, for every language and for all people.
D20 Helpfulness — Caring for people in need.
D16 Responsibility — Teaching others with care.
languageFocus: Every one of the 13 chapters has a Language Focus set built as Notice → Build → Use (4 activities).
Use the Language Focus after basic comprehension and the Quick Challenge.
Always start from the story sentence and ask a meaning question before naming the form.
The Use step is connected spoken or written production about a new, non-story situation.
metadata.differentiationNotes: Reduce linguistic load without lowering the reasoning target: one paragraph at a time, charts given in part, selected vocabulary, audio replay, sentence frames and oral rehearsal. Extend by asking for evaluation, counterpoints and evidence from more than one chapter, not by introducing outside facts.

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: Keep explanations within the wording of the book; do not add outside details or opinions.

Chapter 11 quotes verses of the Qur’an and a hadith with their sources; Chapter 13 gives lines from the Dîvân about the Prophet, prayer and the Miraç. These belong to the teacher-approved text; they are read as they are, without extra comment, and the exercises do not change their words.
Chapters 7 and 10 explain religious concepts such as fenâʾ fillâh, haram, helal and Makasidü’ş-şeria in the words of the book; keep the discussion within these words.
Chapter 9 says that the works are “attributed to” Yesevî and were “probably” written down later; present these as the writer’s careful explanations.
Bracketed Turkish words and the Turkish poem lines belong to the teacher-approved text; they are read as they are.

globalCitizenship.title: Global Citizenship and Cultural Bridges
globalCitizenship.description: Ahmed Yesevî and Hakîm Ata link Central Asia with questions every community faces today: how to teach with simple words, how to do a duty with care and how to welcome guests.

themes.title: Language and identity:
themes.description: Yesevî chose Turkish although he knew Arabic and Persian (Chapter 6). Discuss how languages shape identity in a globalized world.

themes.title: Shared heritage:
themes.description: The mausoleum is a shared cultural heritage of the Turkic-Islamic world (Chapter 5). Discuss how nations can protect a shared heritage.

themes.title: Justice and care:
themes.description: Yesevî warned against corrupt judges and asked people to care for orphans and strangers (Chapter 8). Discuss how communities protect the weak today.

themes.title: Knowledge from every source:
themes.description: The hadith in Chapter 11 encourages embracing useful knowledge regardless of its source. Discuss openness and critical thinking in the age of information.

items.label: D14 Respect
items.value: Respect: Yesevî studied under the leading scholars of his time, is still revered by Turkic peoples and asked people never to harm anyone, even non-believers (Chapters 3, 5, 8 and 13).

items.label: D20 Helpfulness
items.value: Helpfulness: His hikmet speak of caring for orphans and strangers, comforting the heartbroken and standing with the oppressed (Chapters 8 and 13).

items.label: D16 Responsibility
items.value: Responsibility: Teachers must treat students with love and compassion, and Yesevî sent scholars to the scattered tribes (Chapters 6 and 8).

items.label: D3 Diligence
items.value: Diligence: Yesevî received a rigorous education, and the path to fenâʾ fillâh requires education and the discipline of the self (Chapters 6 and 7).

metadata.title: Ahmed Yesevî B2 — Self-Study Guide
metadata.subtitle: Read • Find • Check • Build • Use
metadata.estimatedStudyTime: About 30 minutes per chapter, plus the review pages at the end
metadata.whoIsThisFor: B2 learners who study Ahmed Yesevî alone or with a teacher.
learningGoals: Understand the 13 chapters of Ahmed Yesevî.
Find evidence in the text before answering.
Follow Yesevî’s life, legacy and ideas in extended texts.
Evaluate his ideas about language, wisdom and education with evidence from the book.
Use each chapter’s Language Focus in connected sentences.
recommendedUse: Study one chapter at a time.
Read (and listen, when the audio is ready) before the Quick Challenge.
Repair wrong answers with the text.
Do the Language Focus after you understand the chapter.
Do the review pages after Chapter 13.

readingDiary.intro: Keep this diary when you finish the book. Write short answers.
prompts: The date I finished the book:
My favorite chapter, and one reason:
One idea of Ahmed Yesevî that I think is still relevant today, and why:
One sentence for a friend: “Read this book because …”
One new word I want to keep:
The next book I want to read in the library:

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 13 chapters. Plan the whole book before Chapter 1.
points: Choose your study days and how many chapters you will read each week.
Write one personal goal for this book.
Save new words to My words and review them after one day, three days and one week.

sections.title: 2. One Chapter per Session
sections.text: Each chapter takes about 30 minutes. Open “Study Path” for the steps of your chapter.
points: Preview the title and the “Before You Read” question.
Read for the main idea.
Find the evidence.
Do the Quick Challenge.
Do the Language Focus.

sections.title: 3. Read and Listen
sections.text: Read every chapter twice: once for the main idea, once for the details. When the audio is ready, listen once while you follow the text.
points: First reading: What is the chapter about?
Second reading: Mark names, dates and linking words.
Say one long sentence aloud with the right pauses.

sections.title: 4. Word Notes
sections.text: Bold words have Word Notes. Use them after you have tried to understand the sentence yourself.
points: Guess the meaning from the sentence.
Check the Word Note.
Write the word in a new sentence of your own.

sections.title: 5. Quick Challenge
sections.text: Answer before you read the feedback. If you are wrong, repair the answer with the text.
points: Find the paragraph the question is about.
Read the key sentence again.
Explain why the right answer is right, then try again.

sections.title: 6. Language Focus
sections.text: Each chapter has 4 Language Focus activities built from the chapter’s own sentences.
points: Activity 1 (Notice): Look at a sentence and what it means.
Activities 2–3 (Build): Choose, complete, correct or rewrite forms.
Activity 4 (Use): Write or say connected sentences about a different situation.

sections.title: 7. When It Is Hard
sections.text: Some chapters have many names and dates. Change how you study, not your goal.
points: Read one paragraph only.
Make a time line of the dates.
List the names and what each one did.
Learn only three words today.

sections.title: 8. Values in the Book
sections.text: The book shows respect, helpfulness, responsibility and diligence. Find the sentence first, then think of a small action of your own.
points: Respect: Respect: Yesevî studied under the leading scholars of his time, is still revered by Turkic peoples and asked people never to harm anyone, even non-believers (Chapters 3, 5, 8 and 13).
Helpfulness: Helpfulness: His hikmet speak of caring for orphans and strangers, comforting the heartbroken and standing with the oppressed (Chapters 8 and 13).
Responsibility: Responsibility: Teachers must treat students with love and compassion, and Yesevî sent scholars to the scattered tribes (Chapters 6 and 8).
Diligence: Diligence: Yesevî received a rigorous education, and the path to fenâʾ fillâh requires education and the discipline of the self (Chapters 6 and 7).

sections.title: 9. At the End of the Book
sections.text: After Chapter 13, do the review pages in this order. Go back to a chapter when an answer is not clear.
points: Knowledge Check
Vocabulary Challenge
Master Glossary
Language Review
Final Challenge

sections.title: 10. Look Back
sections.text: Before Chapter 1 and again at the end, answer the “I can” statements of a few chapters. What can you do now that you could not do before?
points: Which chapter changed what you knew?
Explain to someone at home in six sentences who Ahmed Yesevî was and why his ideas still matter, in your home language or in English.
